stem: Why is a proton NMR spectrum usually run in CDCl₃ rather than CHCl₃?

options.content: Deuterium gives no signal, so the solvent does not swamp the spectrum.
options.rationale: Correct: a protonated solvent would swamp the spectrum.

options.content: CDCl₃ reacts with O–H groups in the sample, so they can be identified.
options.rationale: That is the role of D₂O exchange, not of the solvent.

options.content: CDCl₃ provides the reference signal at δ = 0.
options.rationale: The reference is TMS, Si(CH₃)₄.

options.content: CDCl₃ dissolves samples that CHCl₃ cannot dissolve.
options.rationale: Their solvent properties are almost identical; the point is the missing H signal.

explanation: Deuterated solvents contain ²H instead of ¹H, so they give no peak in a proton spectrum.

stem: In the proton NMR spectrum of chloroethane, CH₃CH₂Cl, how is the CH₃ signal split?

options.rationale: A quartet would need three H on the adjacent carbon: that is the CH₂ signal.
A doublet would need one adjacent H.
The CH₃ group has two neighbouring H atoms, so it is split.
Correct: two H on the adjacent CH₂ give 2 + 1 = 3 lines.

explanation: n + 1 rule: CH₃ next to CH₂ (n = 2) → triplet; CH₂ next to CH₃ (n = 3) → quartet.

stem: A sample of ethanoic acid is shaken with D₂O and its proton NMR spectrum is run again. Which signal disappears?

options.content: the CH₃ signal at about δ 2.2
options.rationale: C–H hydrogens do not exchange with D₂O.
TMS has no exchangeable hydrogens.
Correct: the acidic H exchanges with D, which gives no proton signal.

options.content: none, because no hydrogen atom exchanges
options.rationale: O–H hydrogens exchange readily with D₂O.

explanation: CH₃COOH + D₂O ⇌ CH₃COOD + HDO: the O–H signal vanishes.

stem:
Which statements about the proton NMR spectrum of 2-chloropropane, (CH₃)₂CHCl, are correct?

1. There are two signals.
2. One signal is a doublet with relative area 6.
3. The CH signal is a quartet.

options.rationale: Statement 3 is false: the CH has six adjacent H, giving seven lines, not four.
Correct: the six CH₃ protons are split by the single CH; the CH has six neighbours (a multiplet).
Statement 1 is true and statement 3 is false.
Statement 2 is also true.

explanation: Two environments: 6H doublet (CH₃, n = 1) and 1H multiplet (CH, n = 6).
hints: Count the H atoms on the carbons adjacent to the CH.

stem:
Which statements about the proton NMR spectrum of ethanal, CH₃CHO, are correct?

1. There are two signals, with relative areas 3 : 1.
2. The aldehyde H signal is a quartet.
3. The CH₃ signal is a doublet.

Data, δ / ppm: alkane H 0.9-1.7; alkyl H next to C=O 2.2-3.0; alkyl H next to aromatic ring 2.3-3.0; alkyl H next to electronegative atom (O, Cl) 3.2-4.0; H on alkene 4.5-6.0; H on aromatic ring 6.0-9.0; aldehyde H 9.3-10.5; alcohol O–H 0.5-6.0; phenol O–H 4.5-7.0; carboxylic acid O–H 9.0-13.0; alkyl amine N–H 1.0-5.0.

options.rationale: Correct: the CHO proton has three neighbours (quartet); the CH₃ has one neighbour (doublet).
Statement 3 is also true.
Statement 2 is also true.
Statements 2 and 3 are also true.

explanation: CH₃ (3H, doublet, 2.2-3.0) and CHO (1H, quartet, 9.3-10.5).
hints: Apply the n + 1 rule to each group.

stem:
An alcohol, C₄H₁₀O, has a proton NMR spectrum with two singlets: δ 1.3 (relative area 9) and δ 2.0 (relative area 1). The second signal disappears on shaking with D₂O. What is the alcohol?

Data, δ / ppm: alkane H 0.9-1.7; alkyl H next to C=O 2.2-3.0; alkyl H next to aromatic ring 2.3-3.0; alkyl H next to electronegative atom (O, Cl) 3.2-4.0; H on alkene 4.5-6.0; H on aromatic ring 6.0-9.0; aldehyde H 9.3-10.5; alcohol O–H 0.5-6.0; phenol O–H 4.5-7.0; carboxylic acid O–H 9.0-13.0; alkyl amine N–H 1.0-5.0.

options.rationale: This would show five signals with splitting.
Correct: nine equivalent CH₃ protons with no H on the adjacent carbon, plus an O–H.
This would show five signals, several split.
This would show a 6H doublet, a multiplet and a 2H doublet, as well as O–H.

explanation: (CH₃)₃C– gives a 9H singlet (the central C has no H); the O–H singlet disappears with D₂O.
hints: Nine equivalent H with no splitting.

stem:
Compound M, C₃H₆O₂, gives these proton NMR signals: δ 1.2 (3H, triplet), δ 2.4 (2H, quartet), δ 11.8 (1H, singlet, disappears with D₂O). What is M?

Data, δ / ppm: alkane H 0.9-1.7; alkyl H next to C=O 2.2-3.0; alkyl H next to aromatic ring 2.3-3.0; alkyl H next to electronegative atom (O, Cl) 3.2-4.0; H on alkene 4.5-6.0; H on aromatic ring 6.0-9.0; aldehyde H 9.3-10.5; alcohol O–H 0.5-6.0; phenol O–H 4.5-7.0; carboxylic acid O–H 9.0-13.0; alkyl amine N–H 1.0-5.0.

options.rationale: This would give two 3H singlets and no exchangeable H.
No D₂O-exchangeable H; its O–CH₂ quartet would appear above 3.2.
This would show an aldehyde signal at 9.3-10.5 and two CH₂ signals.
Correct: ethyl group next to C=O, plus a carboxylic acid O–H.

explanation: δ 11.8 exchangeable: COOH; quartet + triplet: CH₂CH₃ next to C=O (2.4). M is propanoic acid.
hints: Which signal is an acid O–H?

stem: How many signals are there in the proton NMR spectrum of propanone, CH₃COCH₃?
explanation: All six H atoms are equivalent: one singlet.
workedSolution: 1. All six H atoms are equivalent: one singlet.

stem: How many signals are there in the proton NMR spectrum of butanone, CH₃COCH₂CH₃?
explanation: CH₃CO (singlet), CH₂ (quartet) and CH₂CH₃ (triplet): three environments.
workedSolution: 1. CH₃CO (singlet), CH₂ (quartet) and CH₂CH₃ (triplet): three environments.

stem: How many lines does the CH₂Cl signal of 1-chloropropane, CH₃CH₂CH₂Cl, have?
explanation: The adjacent carbon is the middle CH₂ (n = 2), so the CH₂Cl signal is a triplet.
workedSolution: 1. The adjacent carbon is the middle CH₂ (n = 2), so the CH₂Cl signal is a triplet.
hints: Count the H on the adjacent carbon only.

stem: Pentan-3-one, C₅H₁₀O, gives two proton NMR signals with relative areas 1.5 : 1, in order of increasing δ. How many hydrogen atoms does the signal at higher δ represent?
explanation: 1.5x + x = 10 H, so x = 4: the ratio is 6 : 4. The 4H signal (a quartet near 2.4 ppm) is the two equivalent CH₂ groups next to C=O; the 6H triplet is the two CH₃ groups.
workedSolution: 1. 1.5x + x = 10 H, so x = 4: the ratio is 6 : 4. The 4H signal (a quartet near 2.4 ppm) is the two equivalent CH₂ groups next to C=O; the 6H triplet is the two CH₃ groups.
hints: Scale the ratio so the areas add up to 10.

stem: In the spectrum of ethanol, the CH₂ signal is split into a quartet by the CH₃ group and is not further split by the O–H proton.
explanation: True. The O–H proton exchanges rapidly between molecules, so it does not split the CH₂ signal.

stem: Protons in the same environment split each other's signal.
explanation: False. Equivalent protons do not split each other; splitting comes from non-equivalent protons on the adjacent carbon.

stem: Match each group of protons (in bold) to its splitting pattern.
explanation: Ethyl: CH₃ triplet, CH₂ quartet. Isopropyl CH₃: doublet. CH₃CO: no H on the carbonyl carbon, so a singlet.
hints: n + 1, where n is the number of H on the adjacent carbon.

stem: Complete the sentences about proton NMR.

payload.template: The relative {{blank:a}} of the signals gives the relative numbers of protons in each environment. A signal split into four lines is a {{blank:b}}, showing {{blank:c}} protons on the adjacent carbon.

explanation: Integration gives proton ratios; n + 1 = 4 means n = 3.

stem: Name the compound added to a sample to identify O–H and N–H signals in a proton NMR spectrum.
explanation: Shaking with D₂O exchanges O–H and N–H hydrogens for deuterium; their signals disappear.

stem: Describe and explain how D₂O is used to identify the O–H signal in the proton NMR spectrum of an alcohol.

points.description: Record the spectrum, then shake the sample with D₂O and record it again
The O–H hydrogen exchanges with deuterium: ROH + D₂O ⇌ ROD + HDO
Deuterium does not absorb in the proton region, so the O–H signal disappears (identifying it)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The spectrum is run, the sample is shaken with a little D₂O, and the spectrum is run again. The labile O–H hydrogen exchanges with deuterium (ROH + D₂O ⇌ ROD + HDO). Because deuterium gives no signal in a proton spectrum, the signal that has disappeared is the O–H signal.

explanation: Exchange, then disappearance of the signal.

stem:
Predict the proton NMR spectrum of propanal, CH₃CH₂CHO: for each signal give the δ range, relative area and splitting.

Data, δ / ppm: alkane H 0.9-1.7; alkyl H next to C=O 2.2-3.0; alkyl H next to aromatic ring 2.3-3.0; alkyl H next to electronegative atom (O, Cl) 3.2-4.0; H on alkene 4.5-6.0; H on aromatic ring 6.0-9.0; aldehyde H 9.3-10.5; alcohol O–H 0.5-6.0; phenol O–H 4.5-7.0; carboxylic acid O–H 9.0-13.0; alkyl amine N–H 1.0-5.0.

points.description: CH₃: δ 0.9-1.7, 3H, triplet (next to CH₂)
CH₂: δ 2.2-3.0 (next to C=O), 2H, multiplet (split by CH₃ and CHO; accept quartet of doublets or multiplet)
CHO: δ 9.3-10.5, 1H, triplet (next to CH₂)
Three signals in the ratio 3 : 2 : 1

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Three signals with areas 3 : 2 : 1. CH₃ at 0.9-1.7 ppm, a triplet (two adjacent H). CH₂ at 2.2-3.0 ppm (next to C=O), split by both the CH₃ and the CHO protons, so a multiplet. CHO at 9.3-10.5 ppm, a triplet (two adjacent H).

explanation: Shift, area and splitting for each environment.
hints: The CH₂ has neighbours on both sides.

stem: Explain why the proton NMR signal of the CH₃ group in methyl ethanoate, CH₃COOCH₃, next to the C=O is a singlet.

points.description: The adjacent carbon is the C=O carbon, which has no hydrogen atoms (n = 0)
So by the n + 1 rule the signal has one line (the OCH₃ protons are too far away to split it)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The carbon next to this CH₃ group is the carbonyl carbon, which carries no hydrogens, so n = 0 and the signal is a singlet; the OCH₃ protons are separated by the O and C=O and do not split it.

explanation: No neighbours, no splitting.
hints: Count the H on the adjacent carbon.

stem:
Compound N, C₈H₁₀, is an aromatic hydrocarbon. Its proton NMR spectrum is summarised below.

| δ / ppm | relative area | splitting |
|---|---|---|
| 1.2 | 3 | triplet |
| 2.6 | 2 | quartet |
| 7.2 | 5 | multiplet |

Data, δ / ppm: alkane H 0.9-1.7; alkyl H next to C=O 2.2-3.0; alkyl H next to aromatic ring 2.3-3.0; alkyl H next to electronegative atom (O, Cl) 3.2-4.0; H on alkene 4.5-6.0; H on aromatic ring 6.0-9.0; aldehyde H 9.3-10.5; alcohol O–H 0.5-6.0; phenol O–H 4.5-7.0; carboxylic acid O–H 9.0-13.0; alkyl amine N–H 1.0-5.0.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: What does the signal at δ 7.2 with relative area 5 tell you about N?
parts.explanation: Five H on an aromatic ring: a C₆H₅– group (monosubstituted benzene).

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Explain what the signals at δ 1.2 and δ 2.6 show.

points.description: Triplet (3H) and quartet (2H) together show an ethyl group, CH₂CH₃
The CH₂ at 2.6 is next to the aromatic ring (alkyl next to aromatic ring 2.3-3.0)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: A 3H triplet and a 2H quartet are the signature of an ethyl group: the CH₃ is split by the CH₂ and vice versa. The CH₂ appears at 2.6 ppm, in the range for alkyl H next to an aromatic ring, so the ethyl group is attached to the ring.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: An isomer of N, 1,4-dimethylbenzene, CH₃C₆H₄CH₃, would give which spectrum?

options.content: a triplet, a quartet and a multiplet, areas 3 : 2 : 5
options.rationale: That is the ethylbenzene spectrum.
The CH₃ groups are attached to ring carbons that bear no H, so they are not split.
Correct: six equivalent CH₃ H and four equivalent ring H, with no adjacent H to split them.
The two CH₃ groups are equivalent by symmetry.

parts.explanation: Symmetry gives just two environments, both singlets.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: How many peaks would the carbon-13 NMR spectrum of N show?
parts.explanation: CH₃, CH₂, ring C attached to the chain, ortho (2), meta (2), para: six environments.
parts.workedSolution: 1. CH₃, CH₂, ring C attached to the chain, ortho (2), meta (2), para: six environments.

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem: State the purpose of adding TMS to the sample and why TMS is suitable.

points.description: TMS is the reference: its signal is defined as δ = 0
It gives a single strong peak (12 equivalent H) away from other signals, and is inert and volatile

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: TMS provides the reference signal at δ = 0 against which all shifts are measured. Its twelve equivalent hydrogens give one sharp peak, upfield of almost all others, and it is inert and volatile.

explanation: N is ethylbenzene, C₆H₅CH₂CH₃; 1,4-dimethylbenzene would give two singlets.

stem:
Compound P, C₄H₈O, shows a strong IR absorption at 1715 cm⁻¹ and no broad absorption above 3000 cm⁻¹. Its proton NMR spectrum:

| δ / ppm | relative area | splitting |
|---|---|---|
| 1.1 | 3 | triplet |
| 2.2 | 3 | singlet |
| 2.5 | 2 | quartet |

Data, δ / ppm: alkane H 0.9-1.7; alkyl H next to C=O 2.2-3.0; alkyl H next to aromatic ring 2.3-3.0; alkyl H next to electronegative atom (O, Cl) 3.2-4.0; H on alkene 4.5-6.0; H on aromatic ring 6.0-9.0; aldehyde H 9.3-10.5; alcohol O–H 0.5-6.0; phenol O–H 4.5-7.0; carboxylic acid O–H 9.0-13.0; alkyl amine N–H 1.0-5.0.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: What do the IR data show?

points.description: 1715 cm⁻¹: C=O (aldehyde or ketone)
No broad O–H absorption: not an alcohol or acid

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The strong 1715 cm⁻¹ absorption is a C=O bond, and the absence of a broad band above 3000 cm⁻¹ shows there is no O–H, so P is an aldehyde or ketone.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Explain how each NMR signal fits your structure.

points.description: δ 2.2, 3H singlet: CH₃ next to C=O with no H on the adjacent carbon (CH₃CO–)
δ 2.5, 2H quartet: CH₂ next to C=O, split by a CH₃
δ 1.1, 3H triplet: CH₃ split by the CH₂ (ethyl group)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The 3H singlet at 2.2 ppm is a CH₃ attached to the carbonyl carbon, which has no H, so it is not split. The 2H quartet at 2.5 ppm is a CH₂ next to C=O and next to a CH₃. The 3H triplet at 1.1 ppm is that CH₃, split by the CH₂.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Butanal, CH₃CH₂CH₂CHO, is an isomer of P. Give two differences between its proton NMR spectrum and that of P.

points.description: Butanal shows an aldehyde H signal at 9.3-10.5 ppm (absent in P)
Butanal has four signals (not three) / no 3H singlet (its CH₃ is a triplet)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Butanal shows a 1H signal at 9.3-10.5 ppm from the CHO proton, which P lacks; it has four signals instead of three, and no 3H singlet, because its CH₃ is a triplet at the end of a propyl chain.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: State what would happen to the spectrum of P if it were shaken with D₂O, and why.

points.description: No change, because P has no O–H or N–H hydrogens to exchange

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Nothing would change: P has no O–H or N–H protons, and C–H hydrogens do not exchange with D₂O.

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem: How many peaks would the carbon-13 NMR spectrum of P show?

parts.label: (g)
parts.stem: Explain why proton NMR spectra are run in CDCl₃ and why P's CH₂ signal is a quartet rather than a doublet.

points.description: CDCl₃ contains deuterium, which gives no signal in the proton spectrum, so the solvent does not swamp the sample's signals
The CH₂ is next to a CH₃ (3 H) and next to C=O (no H), so n = 3 and it has 4 lines

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: In CDCl₃ the solvent's hydrogen is deuterium, which does not absorb in the proton region, so the solvent gives no large peak. The CH₂ group has three H on the adjacent CH₃ and none on the carbonyl carbon, so n = 3 and the signal is a quartet.

explanation: P is butanone: CH₃CO (2.2, s, 3H), CH₂ (2.5, q, 2H), CH₃ (1.1, t, 3H).
hints: A 3H singlet near 2.2 ppm suggests CH₃CO–.
